newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close up on German jobless, dollar.
newsitem.headline: French shares close up on German jobless, dollar.

text.p: French shares closed 1.78 percent higher on Wednesday after German data showed a bigger jobless rise than expected.

Brokers said that a rise in July German unemployment, showing economic weakness, would keep the Bundesbank from raising interest rates. Some had been predicting a rate rise due to the mark's weakness against the dollar.
The change of expectations away from a rate rise boosted the Bunds and French bonds and shares followed in their wake.

The gains were further extended in the afternoon because the U.S. dollar weakened on profit-taking. Earlier U.S. economist Fred Bergsten had said the dollar was "way overvalued". Bergsten is a former U.S. Assistant Secretary to the Treasury.
Wall Street, which had opened lower, also forged ahead in early trading.
Better than expected sales figures by French companies also supported Paris shares.
The CAC-40 index closed 1.78 percent or 52.99 points higher at 3,037.09. It had reached a day's high of 3,043.35 and regained in early trading the 3,000 level it had lost on Monday.
August CAC-40 futures ended at 3,045 points, compared to 2,989 at Tuesday's close.
Volume was 8.2 billion francs of which 6.8 billion in CAC-40 stocks.

Bank shares BNP, up 5.45 percent at 290, CCF, up 4.58 percent at 322, and Paribas, up 2.87 percent at 455, made good gains on resurgent takeover rumours following comments by Deutsche Bank that it wanted to grow in France.
Oil stocks Elf, up 2.97 percent at 693, and Total, up 5.30 percent at 636, rose on the back on better-than-expected first half results by British Petroleum Plc.
